title: True-Up Period, Dispositions and Check Minimum — Net Energy Metering Rider Terms
content:
Under every Net Energy Metering rider the credit bank is settled once a year at the true-up and again when the agreement terminates. Each rider fixes the length of the true-up period, how the true-up month is set, the disposition of the bank at each anniversary true-up and at termination, and the smallest payout sent by check.

| Rider | True-up period (months) | True-up month | Anniversary true-up disposition | Termination disposition | Smallest payout sent by check (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rider NEM-L Legacy Net Energy Metering | 12 | Calendar month of the permission to operate date | Cash out | Cash out | 25.00 |
| Rider NEM-R Residential Net Energy Metering | 12 | Calendar month of the permission to operate date | Cash out | Cash out | 25.00 |
| Rider NBT-R Residential Net Billing Tariff | 12 | Calendar month of the permission to operate date | Carry forward | Cash out | 25.00 |
| Rider NBT-C Commercial Net Billing Tariff | 12 | Calendar month of the permission to operate date | Cash out | Cash out | 100.00 |
| Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering | 12 | Calendar month of the permission to operate date | Forfeit | Forfeit | 100.00 |
| Rider NBT-L Large Customer Net Billing Tariff | 12 | Calendar month of the permission to operate date | Cash out | Cash out | 100.00 |

## Points of the terms

- The three dispositions are cash out, carry forward and forfeit. Rider NBT-R Residential Net Billing Tariff is the only carry-forward rider at the anniversary; Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering is the only rider that forfeits, at the anniversary and at termination alike.
- A payout that reaches the check minimum is paid by check; a smaller payout is credited to the service agreement. The minimum is 25.00 under the residential riders and 100.00 under the business riders.
- Hypothetical illustration: an agreement given permission to operate on 14 September has a September true-up month every year.
